entries.title: How are triangles different from one another?
entries.answer: Every triangle has three straight sides and three corners. Some triangles have three equal sides. Others have just two equal sides, or all three sides have different lengths. You can also group triangles by their corners. A right triangle has one square corner, like the corner of a sheet of paper. Each way of sorting helps you describe the same shape in a different way.
facts: The three inside angles of any flat triangle add up to 180 degrees.

questions.text: How can you tell whether a corner is a right angle?
Which shapes have four square corners?
How can a triangle have two matching halves?

entries.title: How can 1/2 and 2/4 be equal?
entries.answer: Draw two strips of the same length. Divide one into two equal parts and shade one part. Divide the other into four equal parts and shade two parts. Both strips are shaded to exactly the same point. That is why 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent fractions. They describe the same amount using parts of different sizes. On a number line, these two fractions also land at the same spot, halfway between 0 and 1.
facts: 3/6 and 1/2 name the same number.
When both the top and bottom numbers are multiplied by 2, the fraction keeps its value.

questions.text: What do the top and bottom numbers in a fraction mean?
How does grouping squares into rows make them easier to count?
What’s a set of steps we could use to compare drawings?

quiz.question: Which fraction lands at the same spot as 1/2?
quiz.explanation: Three out of six equal pieces cover half the whole.

entries.title: How can stacks of dots show measurements?
entries.answer: A dot plot can show measurements along a marked number line. Place one dot above the right number for each measurement. If two leaves are both four centimeters long, put two dots in a stack above four. The tallest stack shows a length that appeared a lot in your collection. A dot alone farther down the line might come from a much longer leaf. You can still see which measurements appeared and how often.
facts: One dot usually represents one observation in this kind of plot.

questions.text: How does a bar graph compare named groups instead?
How can you find the middle measurement in a sorted list?
How many centimeters make up a meter?

entries.title: How can you estimate an answer?
entries.answer: An estimate is a sensible guess based on what you know. Suppose you are adding 29 stickers, 42 stickers, and 38 stickers. They are close to 30, 40, and 40, so you can guess there are about 110. That tells you whether you need a small envelope or a bigger box. If you must give every student the same number of stickers, you can count the exact total before sharing.
facts: An estimate can help you spot an answer far from the right size.

questions.text: How can you pick the nearest ten?
How can a picture help show more information at once?
How can equal groups make the total easier to count?

entries.title: How can you tell how much time has passed?
entries.answer: Elapsed time is how long something lasts from start to finish. Suppose you begin reading at 2:45 and stop at 3:20. Count fifteen minutes from 2:45 to 3:00. Then count the twenty minutes from 3:00 to 3:20. Add those two jumps to find that you read for thirty-five minutes. Splitting the time at a full hour can be easier than comparing the two clock numbers directly.
facts: An hour lasts sixty minutes, so moving forward thirty minutes also moves forward half an hour.

questions.text: How do you read the minute hand of a clock?
What does one half mean as a fraction?
How does a number line show that one point comes before another?

entries.title: How do bars show data?
entries.answer: A bar graph uses bars to show how much is in each group. Imagine surveying a class about favorite fruit. A bar for apples can reach six, a bar for bananas might reach four, and one for grapes eight. Read the group labels and check the numbered scale before comparing the bars. One mark on a scale might stand for one vote, two votes, or another amount.
facts: Bars in one graph use a shared scale, so their lengths can be compared.

questions.text: How can a group of numbers have one typical value?
How can you read a point from two number lines?
Why do useful estimates sometimes give a rough count?

entries.title: How do meters, centimeters, and kilometers fit together?
entries.answer: A meter is a unit of length. A centimeter is one hundredth of a meter, so a meter stick has a hundred centimeters along it. A kilometer is a thousand meters, a useful unit for a trip across town. These units belong to the metric system. Their sizes are related by tens, hundreds, or thousands, so you can switch between units by working with powers of ten.
facts: A centimeter is the length of ten millimeters.

questions.text: Why does moving a digit one place change its value by ten?
How can smaller units help write part of a meter?
How can cubes a centimeter wide measure a box?

entries.title: How do rows help you multiply?
entries.answer: Imagine setting out three rows of four buttons. Each row has the same number, so you can count by fours or multiply three by four. There are twelve buttons. Turn the arrangement sideways and you see four rows of three. There are still twelve. A neat arrangement in equal rows and columns is called an array. Arrays let you see that switching the two numbers in a multiplication gives the same total.
facts: Three groups of four and four groups of three each total twelve.

questions.text: How can rows of square tiles measure space?
How can you turn twelve objects into equally sized groups?
Which pairs of whole numbers multiply to make twelve?

entries.title: How do the faces of a box fit together?
entries.answer: A rectangular box has six flat faces. Each face meets its neighbor along an edge, and three edges come together at a corner. A corner of a solid shape is called a vertex. Opposite faces on the box match in size. On a cube, all six faces match and each one is a square. On many other boxes, a top face and a side face have different shapes or sizes.
facts: A rectangular box and a cube each have twelve edges and eight vertices.

questions.text: How do you measure the amount of room inside the box?
What shape is each flat face of a cube?
How can you count square units on the bottom face?

entries.title: How do you find one point on a grid?
entries.answer: On a simple grid, start where the two number lines meet. The first number in an ordered pair tells you where to go sideways. The second tells you where to go up or down. For the point (3, 2), go three steps right and two steps up. Negative numbers take you left or down instead. Switching the order changes the point. That is why the numbers always go in the same order.
facts: On a first-quadrant grid, the starting point is (0, 0), called the origin.

questions.text: How can a pair of measurements locate a place on Earth?
What numbers can show positions to the left of zero?
How do bars on a graph use a marked scale?

entries.title: How do you find the median?
entries.answer: Put the numbers 2, 6, 7, 10, and 50 in order from smallest to largest. The number in the middle is seven. That is the median. Changing 50 to an even larger number would leave the middle number right where it is. When there are two middle numbers, find the amount halfway between those two. That is the median of the whole list. Ordering the numbers first is what makes the comparison work.
facts: The median of 2, 4, 8, and 12 is 6, halfway between 4 and 8.

questions.text: How is the mean affected by a very large number?
How does putting values in bars help compare them?
When does an estimate make more sense than an exact count?

entries.title: How do you measure area?
entries.answer: Area tells how much flat space a shape covers. Picture a rectangle made of square tiles that all have the same size. If it has three rows with four tiles in each row, it covers twelve square units. You can count each tile or multiply three by four. This works when the squares fill the shape with no gaps or overlaps. Area measures the inside of a shape. If you instead measured all the way around its edge, you would be finding its perimeter.
facts: A square centimeter is the area of a square one centimeter on each side.
A 3-by-4 rectangle covers 12 square units.

questions.text: How can you describe just part of a rectangle’s area?
How can shading two equally sized rectangles show equal fractions?
Why can two flat maps make a country look like two different sizes?

entries.title: How do you measure around a shape?
entries.answer: The perimeter is the distance all the way around a flat shape. Picture a rectangular garden that is six steps long and four steps wide. Walk around its edge, and you go six steps, then four, then six, then four. That makes twenty steps. Measuring the space inside the garden would tell you its area. Perimeter tells you how much fencing might go around it.
facts: If all four sides are five meters long, the perimeter is twenty meters.

questions.text: How do you measure the inside of the same garden?
How do you measure around a circle?
What kind of shape has four equal straight sides and four right angles?

entries.title: How do you measure the space inside a box?
entries.answer: Volume tells you how much three-dimensional space something takes up. Imagine fitting small cubes into a rectangular box. One layer of three rows of four cubes holds twelve cubes. If two layers fit, the box holds twenty-four cubes. Using a cube of a known size, such as one cubic centimeter, gives you a way to describe the amount of space. Bigger cubes would give a smaller count.
facts: The space in a rectangular box can be found by multiplying its inside length, width, and height, using the same unit.

questions.text: How can you count the squares in the bottom layer?
How do equal rows help count the cubes in one layer?
Why can two boxes the same size weigh different amounts?

entries.title: How do you read the hands on a clock?
entries.answer: On many clocks, the short hand shows the hour and the long hand shows the minutes. When the long hand points at the twelve, it is at the start of an hour. Each number farther around counts another five minutes. If the minute hand is at the six, half an hour has passed. The hour hand also moves slowly during that half hour, so it will sit between two numbers.
facts: At 3:30 the minute hand points to six. The hour hand is halfway between three and four.

questions.text: How can you find how many minutes passed between two times?
How much of a circle does the minute hand turn in half an hour?
Why do groups of five minutes make useful multiples?

entries.title: How do you round a number?
entries.answer: Rounding replaces a number with a nearby number that is easier to say or use. To round 47 to the nearest ten, look at 40 and 50. It is seven away from 40 and three away from 50, so 47 rounds to 50. A number exactly halfway between two tens needs an agreed rule. In the usual school rule for whole numbers, 45 rounds up to 50. This rule helps everyone report the same rounded answer.
facts: Rounding 47 to the nearest ten and nearest hundred gives different answers.

questions.text: How do you decide which number should go in the tens place?
How can rounding help you make an estimate?
How can you compare two numbers below 1?

entries.title: How does a protractor measure a turn?
entries.answer: A protractor is a tool with numbers marked around part of a circle. Put its center on the point where the two sides of an angle meet, and line its zero mark up with one side. Follow the other side to see which number it reaches. If the tool has two rows of numbers, choose the row that begins at the zero you lined up. A narrow angle should give a number below ninety.
facts: A half-circle protractor measures turns from zero to 180 degrees.

questions.text: What makes an angle a right angle?
How many degrees do the angles in a flat triangle have altogether?
Why is the line across the middle of a circle special?

entries.title: How far is it around a circle?
entries.answer: Wrap a thread once around the outside of a flat round lid and measure the thread. That gives its circumference. Now measure straight across the lid through the center to find its diameter. The thread is a little longer than three diameters. For every exact circle, the ratio of those lengths is the same. Mathematicians call that number pi, often rounded to 3.14.
facts: A circle with twice the diameter also has twice the circumference.

questions.text: Which measurement goes straight through the center?
What is the distance around a shape with straight sides?
Why can a number like 3.14 be used as a rough value?

entries.title: How is a sphere different from a circle?
entries.answer: A circle is flat, like the outline you draw around the bottom of a cup. A sphere is round in every direction, like a smooth ball. The points on a perfect sphere’s surface are all the same distance from its center. If you could slice an orange right through its middle and look at the cut, the outline would be close to a circle. A slice closer to its skin would be smaller.
facts: A perfect sphere has no flat faces, straight edges, or corners.

questions.text: What is a radius in a flat circle?
What kind of solid has flat circle ends?
Why does the lit part of the Moon change across the month?

entries.title: How likely is something to happen?
entries.answer: Probability tells how likely an event is. A fair coin has two equally likely sides, so the chance it lands heads is one half. That does not say what will happen on the next toss. You might get heads three times in a row. Over many tosses, the share of heads often comes closer to one half. A different game with more possible results might have very different chances.
facts: In a game with equally likely outcomes, a probability of zero means impossible and a probability of one means certain.

questions.text: How do you write one half as a percent?
Why are one half and two fourths the same chance?
What can a repeated sequence tell you about the next item?

entries.title: Is every square a rectangle?
entries.answer: To be a rectangle, a flat shape must have four straight sides and four right angles. A square has all of those things. It has an extra property too: all four sides have the same length. A long postcard is usually a rectangle with two long sides and two short sides, so it is not a square. You can think of a square as one special kind of rectangle.
facts: A square has four sides of the same length, and every corner is a right angle.

questions.text: How can you tell that a corner makes a right angle?
How can you find the distance around a square?
How many matching folds can a square have?

entries.title: What are factors?
entries.answer: Two numbers that multiply to make a whole number are a pair of factors of that number. For twelve, picture rows of buttons. You can make one row of twelve, two rows of six, or three rows of four. These are three different factor pairs for twelve. Arrange the same buttons in five equal rows and some will be left over, so five is not a factor of twelve.
facts: The positive factors of twelve are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 12.

questions.text: How does an array make the pairs easy to see?
What if a number has only one pair of positive factors?
What are the numbers you get by skip-counting?

entries.title: What are multiples?
entries.answer: Count by threes, starting at three. You get 3, 6, 9, 12, and so on. Each of these numbers is a multiple of three because it holds a whole number of groups of three. Zero is also a multiple of three, since it holds zero groups. When you look at a list of multiples of four, some numbers will appear on both lists. Twelve is on both, so it is a common multiple.
facts: Every positive whole number is a multiple of one.

questions.text: How are factors and multiples connected?
Why can the multiples of two all be sorted into pairs?
How does a repeating pattern help you decide what comes next?

entries.title: What are numbers below zero?
entries.answer: You can picture numbers on a line, with zero near the middle. Positive numbers are to the right, and negative numbers are to the left. The number minus three is three steps left of zero. Numbers below zero are handy for things like temperatures on a cold night. A thermometer at minus six degrees reads colder than one at minus two degrees, even though six by itself is larger than two.
facts: Moving right along a number line gives you larger numbers.

How can we show a point sideways and up on a grid?
Where can you place a number like one half?

entries.title: What are the radius and diameter of a circle?
entries.answer: A circle is made of points all the same distance from a center. Draw a straight line from the center to the edge. That line is a radius. Extend that line back through the center until it reaches the opposite edge. The full line across is a diameter, twice as long as the radius. The distance around the curved edge has a different name: circumference.
facts: If the radius is three centimeters, the diameter is six centimeters.

questions.text: How can you measure the distance around a round shape?
What distance would you measure around a rectangle?
Where can you fold a circle to make two halves match?

entries.title: What does a fraction tell you?
entries.answer: A fraction can tell you how much of a whole you have. Cut a sandwich into four equal parts. One part is one fourth, written 1/4. The bottom number, 4, tells how many equal parts make the whole. The top number, 1, tells how many of those parts you are counting. With three parts, you have 3/4. Fractions can also describe amounts bigger than one whole. Five fourths of a sandwich means a whole sandwich and one extra fourth, if the sandwiches are the same size.

sections.heading: Keep the whole the same
sections.text: A half of a large sheet of paper may be bigger than a half of a small sheet. The fractions match, while the sheet sizes differ.

facts: The top number is the numerator.
The bottom number is the denominator.

questions.text: How can two fractions with different numbers be equal?
How can square tiles help measure the amount of a surface?
Why does the place of a digit matter in a number?

entries.title: What does percent mean?
entries.answer: Percent means out of a hundred. Imagine a square marked with a hundred little boxes. If you shade fifty boxes, you shaded 50 percent. That is the same amount as one half of the big square. A hundred percent covers the whole square, and zero percent covers none of it. You can use percent to compare parts of groups even when the groups have different sizes.
facts: A quarter is 25 percent because 25 is one fourth of 100.

questions.text: Why are one half and two fourths equal?
How can you write half using a decimal point?
What fraction of fair coin flips do you expect to be heads over many tries?

entries.title: What does the decimal point show?
entries.answer: In 4.36, the decimal point sits between the ones place and the parts smaller than one. The 4 stands for four ones. The 3 just after the point stands for three tenths, and the 6 farther right stands for six hundredths. Imagine a dollar split into a hundred pennies. Four dollars and thirty-six pennies can be written as $4.36. The decimal point stays after the whole dollars.
facts: Writing 0.5 or 0.50 gives the same number.

questions.text: How can you name three tenths without a decimal point?
Where do equal fractions sit on a number line?
What does half of an amount look like as a percent?

entries.title: What does the mean tell you?
entries.answer: Imagine three friends have two, four, and twelve marbles. Altogether they have eighteen. If they share those eighteen marbles equally, each gets six. Six is the mean of the three original numbers. It helps tell you how much each person would have if the total were shared evenly, even when the real amounts are very different. The mean can fall between numbers in your list.
facts: To find the mean, add the values and divide by how many values there are.

questions.text: How do you find the middle value in a sorted list?
How can bars compare several different amounts?
Why does sharing a whole number sometimes leave something over?

entries.title: What does zero do in a number?
entries.answer: Zero can tell you that there is none of something. An empty basket has zero apples. It also helps show where other digits belong. In 205, the zero shows that there are no tens between the two hundreds and the five ones. If you leave out the zero, 25 means two tens and five ones. Zero is on the number line too, between negative and positive numbers.
facts: Adding zero leaves a number the same.

entries.title: What is a prime number?
entries.answer: Try arranging seven counters in a rectangle with no gaps. You can make one row of seven or seven rows of one, but you cannot make equal rows with both sides greater than one. Seven is prime because its only positive factors are one and seven. Six can make two rows of three, so it is not prime. One is not prime either, since it has just one positive factor.
facts: Two is the only even prime number.

questions.text: How do you find the pairs of factors of twelve?
What happens if you try to pair an odd number of counters?
Why is fourteen a multiple of both two and seven?

entries.title: What is left over after division?
entries.answer: Think of giving seventeen markers to four people. Give each person one, then repeat as long as everyone can get another. Each person gets four markers, and one marker is left. The marker left over is the remainder. What you do with it depends on the question. For markers you can leave one in the box. If you are sharing a cake, you could cut the piece you have left into smaller pieces.
facts: In whole-number division, the remainder must be smaller than the number you divide by.

questions.text: How do equal rows help you check the answer to a division problem?
How do you name the pieces when you split the leftover?
What kinds of numbers can be divided by two with none left over?

entries.title: What makes a can shaped like a cylinder?
entries.answer: A straight circular cylinder has two matching round ends and a curved surface between them. A typical soup can is close to that shape. If you could unroll its side wall onto a table, it would look like a rectangle. One side of that rectangle would be as long as the distance around the round end. The other would measure how tall the can is.
facts: A cylinder like a soup can has two flat circular faces.

How can you compare this can with a box with six flat faces?
What kind of solid has a round base but narrows to a point?

entries.title: What makes a flat shape a polygon?
entries.answer: A polygon is a closed flat shape made by joining straight sides end to end. A triangle is a polygon with three sides. A rectangle has four sides. A circle is flat and closed, but its edge curves, so it is not a polygon. The inside angles and the lengths can change a lot while the shape keeps the same number of sides. That is why two different-looking shapes can still be the same kind of polygon.
facts: An octagon has eight sides, whether or not all those sides are the same length.

questions.text: How do you tell if a shape with four sides is a square?
Why is a circle different from a shape with many sides?
How can you measure the edge around a polygon?

entries.title: What makes a number even or odd?
entries.answer: Put your socks into pairs. If each sock gets a partner, the number of socks is even. If one sock is left without a partner, the number is odd. Fourteen is even and fifteen is odd. Zero is even, because it leaves no sock without a partner. When you look at a whole number written in our usual digits, the last digit tells you whether you can put it into pairs.
facts: A whole number ending in 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8 is even.

questions.text: What does it mean to have one left over after sharing?
Why does the last digit show how many single items there are?
Which numbers have exactly two positive factors?

entries.title: What makes an angle wide or narrow?
entries.answer: An angle shows how far one direction turns from another. Open a book a little. The covers make a narrow angle, smaller than a square corner. Open it until one cover points straight up while the other lies flat. That is a right angle. Open it farther and the angle becomes wider. The amount of turn can change even if both parts of the book are the same size.
facts: A right angle measures 90 degrees.

questions.text: How do the angles inside a triangle fit together?
How do right angles help define a rectangle?
What tool can you use to measure a turn?

entries.title: What makes two halves match?
entries.answer: Draw a heart, then imagine folding it down the middle. If every part of one half lands on the same part of the other half, the fold is a line of symmetry. A shape can have more than one matching fold. A square matches across a fold through the middle from side to side, and also across a fold joining opposite corners. Some shapes have no matching fold at all.
facts: A circle can be folded along any straight line that passes through its center to make matching halves.
A square has four lines of symmetry.

Where is the center of a circle?
How can a set of tiles repeat across a floor?

entries.title: Which part of a calculation comes first?
entries.answer: If you see 2 + 3 × 4, you might think to add first. In the usual order of operations, multiplication comes before addition, so three times four is twelve and the total is fourteen. Put parentheses around 2 + 3 and the instructions change. Do what is inside the parentheses first, then multiply five by four, to get twenty. The symbols let everyone read the calculation the same way.
facts: Multiplication and division have the same rank. When they appear together at that rank, work from left to right.

How can you check a long calculation with a rough guess?

entries.title: Which shapes can tile a floor without leaving gaps?
entries.answer: A tessellation covers a flat surface with shapes that fit just up to one another, without gaps or overlaps. Squares can do it because four square corners meet exactly around one point. Equilateral triangles can do it too. Circles lined up in rows leave curved gaps between them, so circles alone cannot cover a floor without overlap. Tile designs can also use several different shapes together.
facts: Three regular hexagons can meet at a point and fill the space around it.

How do the inside angles of a triangle add up?
How can an artist make tile shapes look like creatures?

entries.title: Why does a digit’s place matter?
entries.answer: In 342, the 3 means three hundreds, the 4 means four tens, and the 2 means two ones. The same digit can be worth a different amount in another place. In 432, the 3 means three tens. You can build these numbers with bundles of sticks. A hundred bundle holds ten bundles of ten, and a ten bundle holds ten single sticks. You can swap ten loose sticks for one ten bundle.
facts: In our number system, each place is worth ten times the place immediately to its right.

What if each place were worth only twice the previous place?

entries.title: Why is an ice cream cone shaped like a cone?
entries.answer: A round cone has a circular base and a surface that gets narrower until it reaches a point. An empty ice cream cone is like the hollow side of that solid shape. A can has two circular ends that stay the same size. A cone’s cross sections parallel to its base get smaller and smaller as you move toward the tip. You can see that difference by comparing water levels inside a cone and inside a straight-sided can.
facts: The single tip of a cone is called its apex or vertex.
